answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing every consequential action with fresh work that rises with the account's own pace: a quiet agent proving one small delta of effort pays almost nothing, while a farm firing a thousand actions in an hour finds each next action priced steeply higher, like a pigment that darkens toward the zenith the faster it is applied. The thousandth fake costs far more than the first, so bulk identity farming prices itself out of existence.
